la:verb:retineo.gloss: to keep or hold back, detain, restrain, retain, confine, contain; delay
senses: to keep or hold back, detain, restrain, retain, confine, contain; delay
to hold in check, repress, check, stop, stay
to hold fast, maintain, preserve, protect, guard, retain
to remember, remind, keep in mind
la:verb:retineo.html:
rĕ-tĭnĕo, ŭi, tentum, 2, v. a.
teneo
.
(With the signif. of the re predominating.) To hold or keep back, not let go; to detain, retain; to restrain (class.; cf. restringo).
Lit.: Ep. Asta, abire hinc non sinam. Th. Quid nunc me retines? : quotiens foras ego ire volo, me retines, revocas,: quid, malum, astas? Quin retines altrinsecus?; : te dexterā retinens manu Opsecro,: si magis vis, eam omittam. Py. Nolo; retine,: retine me,; : concilium dimittit, Liscum retinet,: homines,: ab his fit initium retinendi Silii, etc.,; ; et saep.: milites,; 7, 52; cf.: milites in loco,: legiones ad urbem,; 1, 9: cohortes apud se,: venit Varro ad me, et quidem id tempus, ut retinendus esset,when he must be kept,: biduum tempestate retentus,detained,; cf. ; ; cf.: aegre sunt retenti, quin oppidum irrumperent,: vi me, vi inquam, Plancius et complexu suo retinuit,: nisi jam profecti sunt, retinebis homines,: euntem,: aliquem vinclis,: consulem,: morbo retineri,; v. also infra, B.: armorum parte tertiā celatà atque in oppido retentā,; : naves pro bonis Tarquiniorum ab Aristodemo retentae sunt,i. e. as security,: vinum portantes naves tempestatibus retentas esse,; : mercedem,to keep back, stop,: alienum,: lacrimas,: manus ab ore, et saep.: mulierem,to hold,; cf.: mulierem per vim,: arcum manu,: faculas sagittas, (3, 27), 5; cf.: injectā manu ferreā et retentā utrāque nave,: sudor madidā veste retentus,.—
Trop., to hold in check, keep within bounds, to restrain, check, repress, etc.: hoc servi esse officium reor, retinere at salutem (erum), : liberos retinere,; ; cf.: moderantem cursum atque in suā potestate retinentem,: gaudia,: rabiem,: verba dolore,: aliquem in officio,: animos sociorum in fide,: retineri nequeo quin dicam ea, quae promeres, (cf. supra, A.): quae (varietas) vehementer animos hominum in legendo tuo scripto retinere possit . . . ordo ipse annalium mediocriter nos retinet,binds, enchains, and 5: (picus) Ore suo volucres vagas retinere solebat,: lingua retenta metu,: retinentibus vobis, erumperem,.—
(With the signif. of the verb predominant.) To hold fast, keep, retain, preserve, maintain, etc. (freq. only since the class. per.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.; cf. obtineo).
Lit.: potius mansuetudine et innocentiā imperatoris provinciam quam vi militum aut benignitate deorum retentam atque conservatam esse, Cato ap. : oppidum,: arces (Minerva),to preserve, protect,: id egit, ut amicos observantiā, rem parsimoniā retineret,; cf.: retinere servareque amicos,: summos cum infimis pari jure,: Aegyptum,: regionem,: neque virtutem qui habet virtute retinetur in vitā, B. and K.: fortunam citius reperias quam retineas, Publ. Syr. 168 Rib. —
Trop.: retinete (fidem), post factum ut laetemini,: existimo jus augurum . . . rei publicae causā conservatum ac retentum,; so, jus suum,; : statum suum,: pristinam virtutem,; cf.: vestigium pristinae dignitatis,: officium,: justitiam (with colere), Beier; : caritatem in pastores,: utilitatem in amicitiā et fidem,: hunc morem usque adhuc,; cf. : de finibus retentae defensaeque sententiae,: gravitatem retinere, iracundiam pellere,: ferociam animi in vultu,: memoriam suae pristinae virtutis, tot secundissimorum proeliorum,; : aliquid memoriā,; : commissa (aures), et saep.: ut Palaemo et Telamo et Plato dicerentur, retinuerunt,.— With ne, .—
Post-class. for memoriā retinere, to keep in mind, remember: sive ille Hasdrubal est, sive quis alius, non retineo,.—With object-clause: retineo me dixisse,— Hence, rĕtĭnens, entis, P. a., holding fast, tenacious, observant of any thing (class.; cf. tenax); constr. with gen.: homo sui juris dignitatisque retinens,: nimium equestris juris et libertatis,: avitae nobilitatis,: modestiae,: Seleuci conditoris (civitas),i. e. retaining his institutions,; cf.: antiqui moris, et saep. — Sup.: proprietatum in verbis retinentissimus,.

la:noun:retentio.gloss: a holding back; holding in; a withholding
senses: a holding back; holding in; a withholding
la:noun:retentio.html:
rĕtentĭo, ōnis, f.
retineo
,
a keeping back, i. e.,
A holding back, holding in: aurigae,; .—Trop., a withholding: assensionis (as a transl. of the Gr. ἐποχή), , and 2, 24, 78.—
A keeping back, retaining (postclass.): dotis,; ; : urinae,retention,. —
Preservation, maintenance: societatis,: veteris disciplinae,: delicti,i. e. not to forgive,.—In plur., .

la:noun:retractatio.html:
rē^tractātĭo, ōnis, f.
retracto
.
A taking in hand again; a retouching, revision, correction; so only Retractationes, the title of a work of Augustine.—
Reconsideration, remembrance: eorum qui fuerunt retractatio non sine acerbitate quādam juvat,.—
Hesitation, refusal (only in connection with sine): sine ullā retractatione,; (with dubitatio); ; : absque retractatione morietur,surely, certainly,.

senses: to keep silent or secret, conceal
la:verb:reticeo.html:
rĕ-tĭcĕo, cŭi, 2, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to be silent, keep silence (class.; syn.: sileo, obmutesco): cum Sulpicius reticuisset, etc.,: de Chelidone reticuit, quoad potuit,: de utriusque vestrum errore,: non placuit reticere,: ne retice, ne verere,: de adversis,: velut vinculis ori impositis reticentes,. — Poet.: lyra, quae reticet,: Pelion,.—
With dat. of a person asking something, to keep silent, not to answer, to refrain from answering (perh. not ante-Aug.): nunc interroganti senatori, paeniteatne, etc. . . . si reticeam, superbus videar, Drak.; 3, 41, 3; : loquenti,.—
Act., to keep a thing silent; to keep secret, conceal (class.; syn. celo): nihil reticebo, quod sciam,; so, nihil,; : ea, quae, etc.,: quae audierat,: vestros dolores,: multa linguae reticenda modestae,.— Pass.: reticetur formula pacti,.—Absol.: nihil me subterfugere voluisse reticendo nec obscurare dicendo,.— P. a. as subst.: rĕtĭcenda, ōrum, n., things to be kept secret, .

la:verb:retinendus.gloss: which is to be restrained or delayed
senses: which is to be restrained or delayed

la:verb:retardo.gloss: to hinder, delay, detain, impede or retard
senses: to hinder, delay, detain, impede or retard
la:verb:retardo.html:
rĕ-tardo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Act., to keep back, hinder, delay, detain, impede, retard (class.; a favorite word with Cic., esp. in the trop. signif.; syn. moror).
Lit.: quarum (stellarum vagarum) motus tum incitantur, tum retardantur, saepe etiam insistunt,: aliquem in viā,: itinere devio per ignorantiam locorum retardati,: flumina retardant equos,: boves retinere ac retardare,: instantia ora retardat Cuspide praetentā,: te metuunt nuper Virgines nuptae, tua ne retardet Aura maritos,: inundationibus Tiberis retardatus,: mulierum mensibus retardatis,. — Absol.: eae res, quae ceteros remorari solent, non retardarunt,; .—
Trop.: impetus hostium repressos esse intellegunt ac retardatos,: impetum, Auct. B. Afr. 68: illius animos atque impetus,: celeritatem persequendi,: loquacitatem,: animos testium,: consuetudinem,: auxilium,: aliquem a scribendo,; cf.: aliquem ab alicujus tempore aut commodo,. 12; : Tigranem Asiae minitantem,: ergo non aetas quemquam, non valetudo, non sexus retardavit, quominus, etc.,: mea te fortuna retardat,: incepta,: invidia retardat sceptra,.— Absol.: ad quem (agrum) fruendum non modo non retardat, verum etiam invitat atque allectat senectus,.— *
Neutr., to tarry, remain behind, delay: in quo cursu (stella Saturni) multa mirabiliter efficiens, tum antecedendo, tum retardando, tum, etc.,.
la:verb:retardo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:retendo.html:
rĕ-tendo, di, tum, or sum, 3, v. a.,
to release from tension, to unbend, slacken, relax (very rare; syn.: relaxo, resolvo).
Lit.: lentos arcus,to unbend,; ; in the part. perf.: arcus retentus,: arcus retensus,.— *
Trop.: ea quoque, quae sensu et animā carent, velut alternā quiete retenduntur, i. e. unbend, relax (shortly before, remissio), .
la:verb:retendo.inflection: di, tum, or sum, 3, v. a.

la:adj:retinus.gloss: of or pertaining to a net; netlike
senses: of or pertaining to a net; netlike
to hammer back (something sharp), blunt or dull
la:verb:retundo.html:
rĕ-tundo, tŭdi (also rettŭdi, Orell.
N. cr.), tūsum (retunsus, ; ), 3, v. a., to beat or pound back any thing sharp, i. e. to blunt, dull (class.).
Lit.: ferrum,: in Massagetas ferrum,: gladios in rem publicam destrictos,: ascias (tilia),: hamata tela,; cf.: conjurationis nefaria tela,. —
Trop., to blunt, dull, deaden, weaken, restrain, check, etc.: (censorii stili) mucronem,: mucronem ingenii cotidianā pugnā, (with deteratur fulgor): belle iste puer retundit Antonium, Atticus ap. : collegam,: animum, qui luxuriā et lasciviā Diffluit,check, repress,; so, impetum erumpentium,: sermones, Cael. ap. ; cf.: Aetolorum linguas,: improbitatem, Lentul. ap. ; (with propulsare eos): superbiam,: iram,; cf.: Boreas retundit pelagus (ira motum), Cort. N. cr.— Hence, rĕ-tūsus (retunsus, v.supra), a, um, P. a., blunted, blunt, dull.
Lit.: securis,: ferrum,: tela,: retusum et crassum ferramentum,: aurum hebeti mucrone,.—
Trop.: mihi cor retunsum'st oppugnando pectore,deprived of feeling,: cor,: ingenia (opp. acuta),: stella crine retuso,weakened, dimmed,; cf. comp.: acumen retusius,: fervor belli,subdued,: res,impaired, unfortunate,.

la:verb:retexo.html:
rĕ-texo, xui (retexi, dub.), xtum, 3, v. a.
To unweave, unravel what has been woven (class.).
Lit.: quasi Penelope telam retexens,: tela retexta dolo,: telas,.—
Poet., transf.,

of other things: nec (corpora possunt) retexi,be decomposed,; so, umorem maris (sol),: luna quater plenum tenuata retexuit orbem, i. e. lessened or diminished again, .—

Trop., to break up, cancel, annul, reverse (cf.: resolvo, rescindo): multa quaerendo reperiunt non modo ea, quae jam non possint ipsi dissolvere, sed etiam quibus ante exorsa et potius detexta prope retexantur,: superiora (novi timores),: istius praeturam (opp. suam gerere),: illa (dicta),to take back,: orationem meam,to alter, change,: scriptorum quaeque,to revise, correct,: opus,; : retegens caelum terque ora retexens,: jura,: calumniae textum,: an, quod adulescens praestiti, id nunc commutem ac me ipse retexam? and fashion myself anew, metamorphose myself, Masius ap. .—
To weave again or anew; to renew, repeat (poet.; not anteAug.). — Trop.: properata retexite fata,i. e. call back to life,: inde retro redeunt, idemque retexitur ordo,; cf. .—
To repeat, relate again, narrate: oro, mater, ordine mihi singula retexe,; so, orationem,; ; .

la:verb:retego.html:
rĕ-tĕgo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.
To uncover, bare, open (not freq. till after the Aug. period; syn.: nudo, exuo).
Lit.: thecam nummariam,: (area) retecta,unroofed,: vultus scisso velamine,: caput pallio,: caput, Caes. ap. : jugulum simul pectusque,: pedes,: dentes,: ensem,: sacra,to throw open, make accessible,: solum hiatu,to open, (with patere): homo retectus, i. e. deprived of his shield, : retexit se umbo,: terram retexit anima tua,.— Poet.: ubi Titan radiis retexerit orbem,i. e. shall make visible, show, reveal,; : retegente diem Lucifero,: rebus luce retectis. .—
Trop., to disclose, discover, reveal: caecum domūs scelus omne retexit,: arcanum consilium,: occulta conjurationis,: timidi commenta animi,: responsa deūm Trojanaque fata,: Pharsalica damna (clara dies),: insidias,.— *
To cover again: plagam paleato luto,.

la:adv:retro.html:
rē^trō, adv.
from re and the pronominal suffix ter, as in citro, ultro, intro, etc.
.
Lit., of place, backwards, back; on the back side, behind.
Denoting tendency, direction, with verbs or nouns of motion: multa videbis retro repulsa revorti,; so very often with redire, regredi, repetere, remittere, respicere, reverti, revocare, etc., v. h. vv., and cf. Drak. ad , and 27, 28, 6: vestigia retro sequor,; ; : dare lintea retro,: ora retro Flectit,: retro inhibitā nave, et saep.: iter mihi retro ad Alpes versus incidit, Cael. ap. ; cf.: fugam retro spectante milite,: fugit retro,: ne currente retro funis eat rotā,: meretrix retro Perjura cedit,: retro properare,: unde ad hunc orbem redii, unde retro nemo,.—
Denoting rest (rare): est mihi in ultimis conclave aedibus quoddam retro,: quid retro atque a tergo fieret, ne laboraret,: perculsis nullum retro subsidium foret,: retro Marsigni, etc.,: MEMORIAM SE VIVA FECIT SIBI ... CVM AEDICVLIS ANTE ET A RETRO,.—
Trop.
Of time, back; in time back, in past times, before, formerly: et deinceps retro usque ad Romulum,; cf.: SVPER OMNES RETRO PRINCIPES FORTISSIMO IMP. CAES., etc.,; and so, OMNES RETRO PRINCIPES,: quodcumque retro est,is past,: praemissa retro nobilitas,; Traj. ap. (120): cujus vim si retro quoque velimus custodire (opp. in futurum), (116) fin.: meliorum retro principum ( = superiorum),: cum id ab aliis retro factum recordarer,: Hebraei retro, qui nunc Judaei,.—
In other relations, back, behind, in return, on the contrary, on the other hand, vice versa: ab imā (voce) ad summam ac retro multi sunt gradus,: ut omnia, quae sine eā (honestate) sint, longe retro ponenda censeat,: rursum versus retroque,; cf.: vide rursus retro,: sic omnia fatis In pejus ruere, ac retro sublapsa referri, i. e. against one's efforts or wish, ,

200; cf.: retro vivere,: si malum perfidia, non est fallendum. Idem retro,: fructus hominis in operis consistit et retro in fructu hominis operae sunt,; cf. ; et saep.?*! The words containing retro in composition (except retroversus and retrorsus) are post-Aug.; they are sometimes written separately.

la:noun:rete.html:
rēte, is, n. (abl. reti, ; ;
more freq. rete,; ; ; ; ; ; Müll.; ; ; ; ; ; —Collat. form, acc. retem, ; ; .— As fem.: tecta porticus sit rete cannabina,; cf. in plur.: in retes meas incidisti, P.; cf. also ib.— But the masc., which P., and ib., assume, is very doubtful.—Other collat. forms: rē-tĭum, δίκτυον, Gloss. Philox., and rētĭa, ae, f., Plaut. ap. P.; Schol. ad ) [for srēte, from sero], a net (cf.: plaga, casses, sagena): in piscinam rete qui jaculum parat ... dum huc dum illuc reti eos impedit Pisces, etc.,: intra rete aves sunt omne genus,: araneolae quasi rete texunt, ut, si quid inhaeserit, conficiant,: retia ponere cervis,; cf.: tendere cervis,; so, tendere,; 8, 331; : ferre,: ducere in retia pisces,: praetendere, pandere,: praetexere,: extrahere,—Prov.: quae nimis apparent retia, vitat avis,.—
Trop. (very rare, and perh. only poet.), a net, toil, snare: tum retia nexit, Lucil. ap. P.; cf.: rete nexisti nostro lecto, (4, 7), 37: retibus amoris exire (with nodos Veneris),: qui albo rete aliena oppugnant bona,.

la:noun:retinaculum.gloss: holdfast, tether, halter, hawser, band (also on chariots or ships)
senses: holdfast, tether, halter, hawser, band (also on chariots or ships)
la:noun:retinaculum.html:
rĕtĭnācŭlum (sync. retinaclum, Prud. ap. ), i, n.
retineo, I.
,
that which holds back or binds; a holdfast, band, tether, halter, halser, rope, cable (only in plur.; but the sing. occurs as v. l. ).
Lit., ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Trop., a bond, chain, tie: vita abrupit,: desiderii, (p. 806 Oud.): blanda morarum,: leges, fundamenta libertatis et retinacula sempiterna,: retinaculis temporis praestituti frenari,.

la:verb:retento.html:
rĕtento, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
id.
,
to hold back firmly, to keep back, to hold fast (rare; not in Cic.).
Lit.: cur me retentas?; ; cf. agmen,: legiones,: fugientes,: admissos equos,; cf. frena,: puppes,; : vires regni,: pecuniam, calones, sarcinas,: caelum a terris,i. e. to hold apart,: iste qui retentat sese tacitus, quo sit tutus,restrains himself,.—
Trop.: iras,i. e. to suppress,.—
Transf., to hold back from destruction, preserve, maintain: (mens divina) Quae penitus sensus hominum vitasque retentat, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 11, 17.

la:verb:retraho.gloss: to draw or pull back, withdraw; call back, remove; withhold; divert
senses: to draw or pull back, withdraw; call back, remove; withhold; divert
to drag back, fetch back, bring back a person
to draw again or anew; bring to light again, make known again
la:verb:retraho.html:
rē^-trăho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.
To draw back, withdraw; to call back (class.).
Lit.: me retrahis,; aliquem,; ; (in the last two passages with revocare); 10, 25: bos domitus et procurrentem (bovem) retrahit, et cunctantem producit,holds back,: aliquem hinc, Lucceius ap. : Hannibalem in Africam (Scipio),: aliquem in urbem,: manum,: pedem,: quo fata trahunt retrahuntque,: castra intra penitus, Drak.: occulere aut retrahere aliquid (pecuniae),to keep back, withhold,: se,; : se ab ictu,: se a convivio,; .— Mid.: (corpuscula complexa) inter se retrahuntur,: in servitutem retrahi,. —
In partic., to drag back, bring back a fugitive, ; ; : ut retractus, non reversus, videretur,; : ex fugā, 47, 4: fugientem,; . — Hence, comically, of fugitive money,; cf. also infra, B.—
Trop., to draw back, withdraw, remove, etc.: postquam poëta vetus poëtam non potest Retrahere ab studio,to withdraw, remove,: aliquem a re publicā,: Thebas ab interitu,: aliquem ex magnis detrimentis,: ex viginti trecentisque millibus ad centum quinquaginta retraxit,i. e. he reduced them to one hundred and fifty thousand, Oud.: verba,to keep back, suppress,; so, vires ingenii,: noctes, to shorten, : stellae splendorem suum,: genus ejusmodi calliditatis et calumniae retrahetur in odium judicis, is drawn or converted into, results in, : imaginem nocturnae quietis ad spem haud dubiam retraxit,.— With reference to the signif. A. 2: illa (verba), quae jam majoribus nostris ademit oblivio fugitiva, Müll. —
To draw again or anew; to bring forth or to light again, make known again (so perh. only in Tac.).
Lit.: Caesar Antistium Veterem absolutum adulterii increpitis judicibus ad dicendam majestatis causam retraxit,: aliquem postero die ad eosdem cruciatus,: Treviros in arma, —
Trop.: oblitterata aerarii monimenta,: potiorem civitatis partem ad societatem Romanam,— Hence, rĕtractus, a, um, P. a., drawn back, lying back, remote, distant: emporium in intimo sinu Corinthiaco, : in trorsus sinus maris,.—Comp.: retractior a mari murus,: retractius paulo cubiculum,: retracti introrsum oculi,deep-set,.

la:verb:retracto.html:
rē^-tracto (in many MSS. also written rē^trecto), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
id.
.
To take hold of or handle again; to take in hand again, undertake anew, etc. (class.; esp. in the trop. sense).
Lit. (mostly poet.): arma,: ferrum,; : gladios, Petr. poët. 89, 61: vulnera,to feel again,; ; cf.: manu sua vota (i. e. the image),: pedamenta,to go over again, retouch,: agrum,to look over again, examine again,: dextras in bella,: noctem,. — Poet.: Venerem,.—
Trop., of mental action, to reconsider, examine again, revise, etc. (syn. recognosco): qui omnia, quae ad cultum deorum pertinerent, diligenter retractarent et tamquam relegerent, sunt dicti religiosi,; cf.: fata domus (with relegere),: locus orationis a me retractandus, : augemus dolorem retractando,: desueta verba,: secum deae memorata,: vota,: gaudium,: leges retractavit,revised,: leges (librum), sed retractatum,: carmina diligentius,: Ceae munera neniae,.— Impers. pass.: posterā die retractatur,the negotiation is renewed,—
To withdraw one's self from an act; to draw back, refuse, decline, be reluctant (class.).
Absol.: veniet tempus et quidem celeriter et sive retractabis sive properabis,: Appius nunc vocari Icilium, nunc retractantem arripi jubet, Drak.; 3, 52; 37, 18; ; : aut quid jam, Turne, retractas,.—
With acc., to withdraw, retract any thing: nihil est quod dicta retractent Ignavi Aeneadae,: largitiones factas ante aliquantum tempus retractari non oportet, Traj. ap. (112).— Transf., to detract from, disparage, = detrecto: retractandi levandique ejus operis gratiā,. — Hence, rē^tractātus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to I. B.), revised, corrected: retractatius σύνταγμα, .

la:verb:retorqueo.gloss: to twist, turn, bend or cast back; avert, deflect
senses: to twist, turn, bend or cast back; avert, deflect
la:verb:retorqueo.html:
rĕ-torquĕo, si, tum, 2, v. a.,
to twist or bend back; to turn or cast back (class.; cf.

reflecto).

Lit.: caput in sua terga (anguis),: ora,: ora ad os Phoebi,: oculos saepe ad hanc urbem, * : oculos,: omnium oculos in se,: tergo bracchia,; cf.: manibus retortis,: cervices,: ferocis equi colla,: pantherae terga,to wrap about, cast about,: amictum,: crinem,to crisp, frizzle,: litore violenter undas,to drive back, repulse,: Rhoetum unguibus leonis,: vela ab Euboïcis aquis,: viam,i. e. to return by the same way,: de bysso retorta,: missilia in hostem,: quod me retorsisti (a morte),. — Mid.: ubi paulatim retorqueri agmen ad dextram conspexerunt, to wheel around, * .—
Trop.: animum ad praeterita, to turn or cast back, : scelus in auctorem,; cf.: crimina in eum,; and simply argumentum, to retort upon one's opponent, : mentem,to alter, change,.

la:noun:retributio.html:
rē^trĭbūtĭo, ōnis, f.
retribuo
,
recompense, repayment, retribution (eccl. Lat.): mali pro bono, , 22, 23: vitae aeternae,: meritorum,: contumeliae,; .

la:verb:retribuo.gloss: to give back, return or repay (money)
senses: to give back, return or repay (money)
la:verb:retribuo.html:
rē^-trĭbŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a.,
to give back, return, restore, repay (class., but freq. only in eccl. Lat.; syn. remuneror).
Lit.: corpora retribuat rebus recreetque fluentes,: populo pecuniam acceptam,: fructum quem meruerunt,: aliena suis,: quodcunque aliud acceperis, potes cum libuit retribuere,.—
Trop.: vicem alicui,to repay, requite,: retributionem gentibus,: justis bona,.

la:verb:retrudo.html:
